subject.title: feat(slack): support running as a real Slack user (user identity)

question: Should OpenClaw support a Slack human-user identity whose token grants the agent that user's conversation visibility and posting identity, under an explicit least-scope and preferably dedicated-account contract?
rationale: The Slack platform supports this token model, but accepting the broader human credential and impersonation boundary is a product and security choice rather than a mechanical code-review decision. ([docs.slack.dev](https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/tokens/?utm_source=openai))

options.title: Approve with safeguards
options.body: Accept the mode after the two code blockers are fixed, live DM/MPIM proof is supplied, and dedicated-account and least-scope guidance is explicit.

options.title: Narrow the contract
options.body: Permit the feature only for a dedicated Slack service user and document unsupported use with a person's actively used account.

options.title: Keep bot identity only
options.body: Decline the human-token mode and retain the existing bot plus read-only user-token model.

recommendation.title: Approve with safeguards
recommendation.body: Accept the mode after the two code blockers are fixed, live DM/MPIM proof is supplied, and dedicated-account and least-scope guidance is explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository identifies him as product owner, and he authored the proposed product and credential model. ([github.com](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md?utm_source=openai))
